reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a walkthrough of a Solana DeFi yield aggregator, showing how to filter vaults and inspect APY, TVL, categories, and historical performance. Although it includes return figures, vault links, and deposit descriptions, the available video evidence characterizes these as an ordinary product demonstration without establishing deception or guaranteed future returns. It also does not establish that viewers transferred funds or that any external vault produced particular results.

opening.argument: Judge, the invitation is tied directly to a financial return: viewers are told to explore the tool and use its filters to make their APY go up. The description supplies the tracker destination, while the displayed vault pages pair APY figures with a “Go to Vault” button. That sequence matters. It moves the viewer from seeking a higher yield, to selecting a vault, to a link for participating in it. The video does not merely define APY; it urges viewers toward yield-bearing vaults.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this a walkthrough of filters and historical performance, but those features also make the yield pitch actionable: viewers can narrow the choices before following a vault link. The invitation to explore is not detached from the stated goal of increasing APY. Nor does the absence of evidence that anyone transferred funds settle what the video asks viewers to pursue.

citations.quote: You can filter everything, all underlying assets, all categories, and even filtered by protocol.
find new opportunities that you didn't know just by filtering and go deep here to make that apy that you are getting go up.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A route from research to a vault is not, by itself, evidence of a scam. The speaker presents the tool as a way to compare data and inspect APY over time, and explicitly directs viewers to learn more about a vault. The cited language encourages exploration and a higher APY; it does not promise a fixed return, conceal a loss, or show that any viewer deposited funds.

citations.quote: we have here the APY history, we can open it for example GLP and we have the TBL of that concrete bolt over time and the APY over time over it
And all the relevant links that will teach us more about the vault whenever we need to learn about it.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals together. The tracker prominently displays vault APYs above 50%, with an entry at 85.19%, and a vault detail page offers a “Go to Vault” button beside a performance chart. The description frames the endpoint as maximizing Solana returns, while the speaker says the tool can help viewers make their APY go up. Historical charts do not verify future income. In this setting, prominent high yields, an external destination, and a direct vault pathway make the presentation a return-driven solicitation, not just neutral market information.

citations.quote: 02:23 OUTRO: Start Maximizing your Solana Returns
go deep here to make that apy that you are getting go up.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense points to APY history as evidence of education. But a history chart does not establish that the prominently displayed yields can be sustained. Likewise, sorting by APY and TVL can guide viewers toward a high-yield vault without establishing the risks behind that yield. The objection is to the combined presentation and pathway, not a claim that the video proves anyone earned or lost money.

citations.quote: But basically you have the list of boltss ordered by APY. You can order them by TBL as well.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: High displayed APYs and links warrant scrutiny, but the cited material does not establish deception. The interface also shows differing yields and performance histories, including a chart that changes over time. The speaker describes comparing vault data and learning about individual vaults. Neither the figures nor the call to explore promises that a viewer will receive those returns.

citations.quote: And all the relevant links that will teach us more about the vault whenever we need to learn about it.

opening.argument: Judge, the tutorial format is also the means of promotion. The speaker says “we have built” the tracker, walks viewers through its filters, and closes by telling them to use it to find opportunities and raise their APY. The description gives a direct tracker link, and the demonstrated vault page contains a “Go to Vault” control. The lesson is therefore not independent analysis of whether a particular return is attainable; it is a guided path from the presenter’s tool toward yield-bearing vaults. That promotional purpose should carry weight when assessing the return-focused message.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense accurately describes the filtering and vault descriptions, but those details do not make the presentation independent. The presenter identifies the tracker as something “we have built,” then encourages viewers to use it to find opportunities. The defense also notes that transfers and outcomes are unproven; promotion can steer viewers toward participation before any transfer or outcome is visible.

citations.quote: And that's why we have built LINZ gel tracker.
So I got the tool for you now it's your time to actually go deep, save those hours for sure.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The promotional role is visible, but promotion is not proof of fraud. The speaker demonstrates sorting, filters, vault histories, descriptions, and links for further research. The prosecution identifies a pathway to vault information, yet cites no false claim, guaranteed return, or evidence that the tracker misrepresents a vault. On this record, the demonstrated function remains a yield-research tool.
